title: Orthostochastic Residual Mixing for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections

contributions.purpose: Provide a simpler alternative to Sinkhorn-Knopp projection for enforcing doubly stochastic residual mixing matrices in mHC.
contributions.mechanism: Construct orthostochastic H_res matrices by orthogonalizing unconstrained logits with Newton-Schulz iteration (15 steps, coefficients (3.0, -3.2, 1.2)) and then entrywise-squaring the resulting orthogonal matrix (O = Q ⊙ Q), which is doubly stochastic by construction.
contributions.evaluation: Constraint fidelity: DS error ~0.006 and orthogonality residual ~0.008, both well below the 10^-2 threshold, consistent across n=4 and n=8.
contributions.domain: Deep learning architecture / residual connections for language model pretraining
contributions.source_quote: We propose orthostochastic H_res construction for mHC, using Newton-Schulz iteration followed by entrywise squaring to produce doubly stochastic matrices with exact constraint satisfaction.

contributions.purpose: Empirically test whether the reduced-expressiveness orthostochastic subset suffices for effective residual mixing.
contributions.mechanism: Compare orthostochastic mHC against Sinkhorn-projected mHC and unconstrained HC on nanoGPT/FineWeb pretraining in two settings (48L n=4; 6L n=8).
contributions.evaluation: At n=4 val-loss gap is +0.003 (within 0.5σ, statistically equivalent); at n=8 a gap of +0.013 emerges (between 0.5σ and 1.0σ); both mHC variants cut gradient spike ratio ~39-40% vs unconstrained (rmax 1.87/1.91 vs 3.14).
contributions.domain: Deep learning architecture / residual connections for language model pretraining
contributions.source_quote: At n = 4 residual streams, orthostochastic matches Sinkhorn (∆ = +0.003 validation loss, within 0.5σ); at n = 8, a small gap emerges (∆ = +0.013, between 0.5σ and 1.0σ), consistent with reduced expressiveness at larger n.

contributions.purpose: Explain why the reduced expressiveness of orthostochastic matrices does not hurt performance.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze training dynamics of the learned H_res matrices for both Sinkhorn and orthostochastic mHC.
contributions.evaluation: Both methods converge to near-identity H_res matrices (Sinkhorn to exact identity; orthostochastic ||H_res - I|| in [0.001, 0.166]), implying mHC's benefit is from stability guarantees rather than exploiting the Birkhoff polytope interior.
contributions.domain: Deep learning architecture / residual connections for language model pretraining
contributions.source_quote: We find that both methods converge to near-identity H_res matrices during training, suggesting that mHC's benefits arise from stability guarantees rather than exploiting the full Birkhoff polytope interior.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) (Xie et al., 2026) address this by constraining the residual mixing matrix H_res to be doubly stochastic ... The standard approach ... is Sinkhorn-Knopp projection ... This motivates exploring simpler alternatives ... We investigate orthostochastic matrices ... constructed via Newton-Schulz iteration (Grishina et al., 2025; Amsel et al., 2025).
Our work connects these two lines by using orthogonal matrices to construct orthostochastic matrices, which form a subset of doubly stochastic matrices with exact constraint satisfaction.
To construct orthostochastic H_res matrices, we employ Newton-Schulz iteration (Liu et al., 2025; Amsel et al., 2025) to orthogonalize unconstrained logits, followed by entrywise squaring.

notes: The proposed method does not beat the Sinkhorn baseline: it is statistically equivalent at n=4 and slightly worse at n=8; the paper frames it as a viable alternative rather than an improvement.
